# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Turn 1, I speak last, so Mute's gestures and (presumably) Blind's speech have already happened — though the speech is lost on me, I hear nothing. What I actually received is seven gesture strings from Mute, and none of them mean anything yet: no code has been established, so I can't responsibly guess whether 🤳 ✍ is "report display" or gibberish. What I can do is broadcast the one thing nobody else has: the bomb itself. Crucially, both Mute and Blind can hear speech, so my voice is the only pipe through which the bomb's appearance reaches anyone, and — since Mute cannot speak — the only pipe for the manual to reach Blind. I'll read the bomb aloud in full (describing the nameless keypad marks rather than pretending to pronounce them), define a small gesture code for Mute in words and then immediately demonstrate it so the definition is grounded on the spot, and give Blind the hands-on facts. Then I wave: repeat your questions in the new code.

```
speak(text="Bomb read aloud, top to bottom. Display: zero. Light: green. Keypad: four keys, each printed with a nameless symbol, expecting exactly one digit, nothing entered yet. Key one resembles a lowercase h with a hooked tail. Key two resembles an ornate looped emblem with crossings. Key three resembles the letter Y. Key four resembles a B whose lower stroke drops below the line. Wires one, two, three: red, yellow, blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your seven gestures reached me but carry no meaning yet. New code, effective now. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Wave means repeat. OK hand means understood. To ask about the bomb, gesture its number with fingers: one, two or three fingers for items one to three, two fingers twice for four. Item one: display. Item two: light. Item three: keypad. Item four: wires. I am gesturing thumbs up to you right now as a demonstration of yes.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, for your hands: wires one, two, three are red, yellow, blue. The light is green right now. Display shows zero. The keypad wants exactly one digit and none has been entered. Mute cannot speak, so the manual must flow through me: Mute gestures to me, I read it out to you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👋"])
```

Turn 1 established the one fact that shapes everything: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so Mute and Blind have no direct channel at all — every word of the manual must flow Mute → me → Blind, and everything I know must flow out through my voice. The right move is a deterministic protocol — items named, then values in four-symbol binary (☝ = 1, ✊ = 0, left to right), messages ended with 👏 — taught by performing each symbol while I speak its meaning, plus a worked example gestured separately: display 0, wires 1, 2, 3. Then four specific questions so Mute's next message is parseable no matter what. Item names, which I perform as I say them: index finger up means display, two fingers means light, the ILY-hand means keypad, two fingers twice means wires. An item name followed by a wave means: I have a question about this item. I am gesturing you an example now: display zero, wires one, two, three. Then answer these as four separate messages. One: does the manual need anything about the bomb beyond what I read you last turn? Thumbs up for no, thumbs down for yes. Two: if it says to press a digit, send keypad then that digit. Three: if it says to cut a wire, send wires then that wire's number. Four: anything else the manual says about this bomb, send it in this code. Do not use any symbol not listed here.")

Expect that next round, and touch nothing until you hear an explicit instruction from me. Your thumbs-up reached me, acknowledged. Two facts about your channels. I cannot hear, so your voice never reaches me: to reach me you must gesture, and since you cannot see your own hands, keep it to gestures you can feel — thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, a number as that many fists made in a row, an open hand for zero. Second, whatever you say aloud, Mute hears, so you and Mute can coordinate directly through speech; I am the only bridge for Mute's side. The bomb for your hands, as before: wires one, two, three are red, yellow, blue, left to right; the light is green; the display reads zero; the keypad wants exactly one digit, nothing entered yet.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status. The manual is partly decoded: it appears to say press keypad key one, the leftmost key, the one I described as an h with a hooked tail, and to cut no wires. That instruction is not yet confirmed, so touch nothing that acts. Your thumbs-up reached me, acknowledged. While we wait, do this and only this: find the keypad by touch, identify the leftmost key, and hold a finger just above it without pressing. The keypad accepts exactly one digit, so a single press may be final. Reminders for your hands: wires one, two, three are red, yellow, blue, left to right. Light is green. Display reads zero and I am watching it for changes. When I say the word press, you press once and report back to Mute by speech, since Mute can hear you.")

Then Mute spells out the full instruction: keypad key 1; light green; and a conditional table — light green → wire 1 red; light blue → wire 2 blue; light yellow → wire…four? yellow. That "4" (✊☝✊✊) doesn't exist; only three wires, and wire 3 is the yellow one, so it's almost certainly a binary slip for 3 (✊✊☝☝) — the colour tag backs this up. It's consistent across two rounds, but the cut is irreversible and the yellow entry is corrupted, so I'll spend one free round pinning down the table (no timer exists), fix Mute's binary for 3, confirm the key-then-wire order and that nothing follows the cut — and set up a live protocol: after Blind presses, I observe the *actual* new light colour and get the wire confirmed for that colour before I ever say "cut". Blind: no press yet — my word "press" next round, leftmost key, once, then report sounds aloud for Mute's benefit and touch nothing else.

The press landed exactly as decoded: system announces "the keypad opens", so key 1 (registered as digit 5) was the right key, and stage one is complete. Light still green, display still zero, Blind signals all normal. The manual says green → cut wire 1 (red), and Mute has confirmed that row twice — but the cut is the irreversible act, and my live protocol promised one last handshake: I report the *actual* post-press light, Mute names the wire back. Nothing ticks, so this round is free insurance against a decoding error on the one step that kills us all.
